claims.text: Pectoral girdle: the clavicle and scapula attach the upper limb to the sternum of the axial skeleton.
claims.quote: The pectoral girdle consists of the clavicle and the scapula, which serve to attach the upper limb to the sternum of the axial skeleton.

claims.text: Clavicle: the only long bone that lies horizontally in the body.
claims.quote: The clavicle is the only long bone that lies in a horizontal position in the body

claims.text: Sternal end: the medial end of the clavicle articulates with the manubrium of the sternum.
claims.quote: The medial end, known as the sternal end of the clavicle, has a triangular shape and articulates with the manubrium portion of the sternum.

claims.text: Arm and forearm: the humerus is the single bone of the upper arm; in the forearm the ulna is medial and the radius lateral.
claims.quote: The humerus is the single bone of the upper arm, and the ulna (medially) and the radius (laterally) are the paired bones of the forearm.

claims.text: Surgical neck: a common site of humerus fractures.
claims.quote: The surgical neck is a common site of arm fractures.

claims.text: Wrist and palm: eight carpal bones form the base of the hand and five metacarpals form the palm.
claims.quote: The base of the hand contains eight bones, each called a carpal bone, and the palm of the hand is formed by five bones, each called a metacarpal bone.

claims.text: Fingers: 14 phalanges in the fingers and thumb.
claims.quote: The fingers and thumb contain a total of 14 bones, each of which is a phalanx bone of the hand.

claims.text: Carpal bones: “So Long To Pinky, Here Comes The Thumb” names the proximal row lateral to medial (scaphoid, lunate, triquetrum, pisiform), then the distal row medial to lateral (hamate, capitate, trapezoid, trapezium).
claims.quote: A helpful mnemonic for remembering the arrangement of the carpal bones is “So Long To Pinky, Here Comes The Thumb.” This mnemonic starts on the lateral side and names the proximal bones from lateral to medial (scaphoid, lunate, triquetrum, pisiform), then makes a U-turn to name the distal bones from medial to lateral (hamate, capitate, trapezoid, trapezium).

claims.text: FOOSH: a hard fall onto an outstretched hand can fracture the humerus, radius or scaphoid.
claims.quote: Many fractures result from a hard fall onto an outstretched hand. The resulting transmission of force up the limb may result in a fracture of the humerus, radius, or scaphoid bones.

claims.text: Carpal tunnel: nine tendons and a major nerve pass through it; the carpal bones form its walls and floor and the flexor retinaculum its roof.
claims.quote: The carpal tunnel is the passageway by which nine muscle tendons and a major nerve enter the hand from the anterior forearm. The walls and floor of the carpal tunnel are formed by the U-shaped grouping of the carpal bones, and the roof is formed by the flexor retinaculum, a strong ligament that anteriorly unites the bones.
